content.value_statement: Creating a skill can be difficult when its files, metadata, and references are unclear. This guide explains a practical structure for authoring organized Claude Code skills.
actual_capabilities: Explains the required SKILL.md file and YAML front matter.
Shows basic and extended directory structures for skills.
Describes personal and project-level skill locations.
Illustrates references to supporting documentation and helper scripts.
Lists documented size, metadata, and reference-depth guidance.
limitations: The guide is primarily written in Chinese.
It provides guidance rather than creating files automatically.
It does not validate a finished skill.
It does not cover every Claude Code skill feature or tool integration.

use_cases.title: Start a personal skill
use_cases.description: Set up a personal skill directory and create the required SKILL.md structure.

use_cases.title: Standardize project guidance
use_cases.description: Organize project-specific skills with references, examples, and optional helper scripts.

use_cases.title: Plan a larger skill library
use_cases.description: Use progressive disclosure and functional folders to keep several related skills maintainable.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: create a basic skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this guide to help me create a basic Claude Code skill named Writing Documentation. Draft the SKILL.md metadata and sections.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: choose a location
prompt_templates.prompt: Based on this guide, explain whether I should store my new skill in my personal Claude directory or in this project.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: add references
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me organize a Claude Code skill with SKILL.md, reference.md, examples.md, and one helper script. Explain what belongs in each file.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: design a skill collection
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a maintainable folder structure for skills covering code review, documentation, PDF processing, and spreadsheet analysis. Use progressive disclosure.

output_examples.input: I need a personal skill for testing code.
output: Required file: SKILL.md with a name and description.
Add reference files only when detailed guidance is needed.

output_examples.input: How should I organize a skill with detailed examples?
output: Keep the main instructions in SKILL.md.
Link to examples.md from SKILL.md when users need it.

best_practices: Use a specific action-oriented name and a clear description.
Keep primary instructions concise and place detailed material in referenced files.
Store project-specific skills in the project directory so collaborators can use them.
anti_patterns: Do not use vague names such as Helper or Tools.
Do not put all reference material into SKILL.md when it can be loaded only when needed.
Do not create deeply nested chains of reference files.

faq.question: What file does every skill require?
faq.answer: Every skill requires a SKILL.md file with YAML front matter.

faq.question: Where can I store a personal skill?
faq.answer: Store it under ~/.claude/skills/ in a directory for that skill.

faq.question: Where can I store a project skill?
faq.answer: Store it under .claude/skills/ inside the project.

faq.question: Can a skill include helper scripts?
faq.answer: Yes. The guide shows an optional scripts directory for utility scripts.

faq.question: What is progressive disclosure?
faq.answer: Keep primary instructions in SKILL.md and load supporting files only when they are needed.

faq.question: Does this guide create or validate skills automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides authoring guidance and example structures.
